answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with bond-backed claims viewed through a prism of open audit: every service claim carries a small refundable deposit, like ivory tokens placed on a jetty before a boat may dock. Any peer may challenge a claim with evidence; a false claim forfeits its bond to the challenger, while true claims are refunded. A farmer running a thousand fakes must fund a thousand forfeitable bonds, and each exposed fake pays its detector, so mass fakery becomes expensive and self-defeating.
